==Characteristics==
Knuckles is an anthropomorphic red short-beaked echidna, the only living descendant of a well-established clan of echidnas.<ref name="EUR profile"/> For many years, his clan guarded a giant gemstone called the Master Emerald, which controls the [[Chaos Emeralds]], objects central to the ''Sonic the Hedgehog'' game series.<ref name="jp profile">{{cite web |url=http://sonic.sega.jp/chara/Knuckles/index.html |script-title=ja:ナックルズ・ザ・エキドゥナ|language=ja|publisher=Sonic.sega.jp|access-date=January 8, 2007|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20061231041629/http://sonic.sega.jp/chara/knuckles/index.html |archive-date=December 31, 2006}}</ref> As such, Knuckles has spent most of his life atop a [[Floating island (fiction)|floating island]] called Angel Island, guarding the Master Emerald from harm.<ref name="Sonic Adventure 2 profile">''[[Sonic Adventure 2]]'' (Dreamcast) [https://www.gamesdatabase.org/Media/SYSTEM/Sega_Dreamcast//Manual/formated/Sonic_Adventure_2_-_2001_-_Sega.pdf instruction manual] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200607211105/https://www.gamesdatabase.org/Media/SYSTEM/Sega_Dreamcast/Manual/formated/Sonic_Adventure_2_-_2001_-_Sega.pdf |date=2020-06-07 }}, pp. 10–11. (PDF)</ref> He has grown up fairly [[extraversion and introversion|introverted]] as a result.<ref name="EUR profile"/>

Knuckles has a personality described as cool.<ref name="Sonic Central"/> However, he sometimes loses his composure and gets in fights with [[List of Sonic the Hedgehog video game characters|other characters]], and he can be shy around girls.<ref name="Sonic Jam profile">[[Sega]] (1997). ''[[Sonic Jam]]'', Sega Saturn. Sonic World's Character Profiles (in [[English language|English]])</ref> His favorite food is [[grape]]s, and his relationship with [[Sonic the Hedgehog (character)|Sonic]] is ambivalent. However, in later games, their relationship became more unequivocal: Knuckles entered the series as an antagonist of Sonic but later becomes one of the protagonists and sees him as a partner,<ref name="GSpy Naka">{{cite web |url=http://ps2.gamespy.com/articles/654/654749p1.html |last=Kemps |first=Heidi |title=Sega's Yuji Naka Talks! |access-date=October 26, 2014 |publisher=[[GameSpy]] |date=September 30, 2005 |archive-date=June 24, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090624050230/http://ps2.gamespy.com/articles/654/654749p1.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Advance 3"/><ref name="Heroes">[[Sega]] (2003). ''[[Sonic Heroes]]'' [https://www.gamesdatabase.org/Media/SYSTEM/Sony_Playstation_2//Manual/formated/Sonic_Heroes_-_2003_-_Sega.pdf instruction manual] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190630101349/https://www.gamesdatabase.org/Media/SYSTEM/Sony_Playstation_2/Manual/formated/Sonic_Heroes_-_2003_-_Sega.pdf |date=2019-06-30 }}, pp. 7–8. (PDF)</ref> while envying Sonic's adventurous lifestyle.<ref name="Sonic Central">{{cite web|author=Sega of America |publisher=Sega.com |url=http://www.sega.com/sonic/globalsonic/post_allabout.php?article=soniccharacters |title=Sonic's official character profile from Sega of America |access-date=March 10, 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090217221441/http://www.sega.com/sonic/globalsonic/post_allabout.php?article=soniccharacters |archive-date=February 17, 2009 }}</ref> He is depicted as somewhat gullible and very rash, especially when angered.<ref name="jp profile"/><ref name="bright"/> Knuckles has often been tricked by [[Doctor Robotnik]] due to his naivety, but is stated in one game manual to have become more skeptical of him, possibly due to the multiple times of getting fooled by Robotnik.<ref>''[[Sonic Riders: Zero Gravity]]'' (Wii) instruction manual, p. 4.</ref>

While slower than Sonic, Knuckles is depicted as one of the series's strongest characters and a skilled [[martial arts|martial artist]]: his brawny physique allows him to lift objects many times his size and weight, while his powerful fists enable him to smash boulders and break through solid ground.<ref name="EUR profile">{{cite web |url=http://www.sonic-city.com/en/characters/knuckles/index.html |title=Sonic City |access-date=March 4, 2008 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080225070243/http://www.sonic-city.com/en/characters/knuckles/index.html |archive-date = February 25, 2008 |author=<!-- not stated --> |website=sonic-city.com |publisher=[[SEGA]] }}</ref><ref name="jp profile"/> He can also glide long distances and climb up walls using the spikes of his gloves.<ref name="jp profile"/> Unlike Sonic, Knuckles is able to swim.<ref name="Advance 3">[[Sega]] (2004). ''[[Sonic Advance 3]]'' instruction manual, pp. 12-13.</ref> As is typical among ''Sonic'' characters, Knuckles can roll into a ball to attack enemies.<ref name="Sonic & Knuckles">[[Sega]] (1994). ''[[Sonic & Knuckles]]'' [https://www.digitpress.com/library/manuals/genesis/sonic%20&%20knucles.pdf instruction manual] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220121100747/https://www.digitpress.com/library/manuals/genesis/sonic%20%26%20knucles.pdf |date=2022-01-21 }}, pp. 7–8. (PDF)</ref> He also has an empowered "[[Super transformation (Sonic the Hedgehog)|super]]" form: using the Chaos Emeralds allows him to transform into Super Knuckles. Using the Super Emeralds allows him to transform into Hyper Knuckles.<ref name="chronicles super">{{cite video game|title=[[Sonic Chronicles: The Dark Brotherhood]] |developer=Bioware |publisher=Sega |platform=Nintendo DS |level=Codex }}</ref>

==Appearances==

===In video games===
Knuckles debuted in the 1994 [[Sega Genesis]] game ''Sonic the Hedgehog 3''. Knuckles joins the series's primary antagonist Dr. Robotnik after being tricked into thinking that Sonic is attempting to steal the Master Emerald; Knuckles fights Sonic at several points throughout the game. Robotnik's betrayal is revealed late in ''[[Sonic & Knuckles]]'' when he steals the Master Emerald and attacks Knuckles, ''[[Sonic & Knuckles]]'' is also the first game where he became a player character, his story takes place after ''Sonic's Story''.<ref name="ign sand"/> A similar plot follows in ''[[Sonic the Hedgehog: Triple Trouble]]''. While Knuckles's canonical playable debut comes in ''Sonic & Knuckles'', he is playable in ''[[Sonic the Hedgehog 2|Sonic 2]]'' and ''3'' via the Genesis' [[Sonic & Knuckles#Lock-on technology|lock-on technology]].<ref name="ign sand">{{cite web|last=Thomas|first=Lucas M.|url=http://www.ign.com/articles/2010/02/22/sonic-knuckles-review|title=Sonic & Knuckles Review|website=[[IGN]]|date=February 22, 2010|access-date=March 13, 2014|archive-date=July 14, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150714200548/http://www.ign.com/articles/2010/02/22/sonic-knuckles-review|url-status=live}}</ref> Knuckles starred in ''[[Knuckles' Chaotix]]'' for the [[Sega 32X]], in which he serves as the guardian of an island [[amusement park]] and rescues his friends—collectively known as the [[Chaotix]]—from Robotnik in 1995. He teams up with them individually, creating an unusual gameplay style involving two characters being tethered together.<ref>''[[Knuckles' Chaotix]]'' [https://www.gamesdatabase.org/Media/SYSTEM/Sega_32X//Manual/formated/Knuckles-_Chaotix_-_1995_-_Sega.pdf instruction manual] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190328214947/https://www.gamesdatabase.org/Media/SYSTEM/Sega_32X/Manual/formated/Knuckles-_Chaotix_-_1995_-_Sega.pdf |date=2019-03-28 }}, p. 2. (PDF)</ref>

Eggman shatters the Master Emerald, thus freeing [[Chaos (Sonic the Hedgehog)|Chaos]] who appears before Knuckles, the pieces are scattered around, and Chaos flees in ''[[Sonic Adventure]]''.<ref>{{cite video game|title=[[Sonic Adventure]]|developer=[[Sonic Team]]|publisher=Sega|date=September 9, 1999|quote=Knuckles: Something's happened to the Master Emerald!}}</ref> To restore the Emerald, thereby protecting Angel Island,<ref>{{cite video game|title=Sonic Adventure|developer=Sonic Team|publisher=Sega|date=September 9, 1999|quote=Knuckles: Without the Master Emerald's power, this whole island will fall into the ocean!}}</ref> he searches through various expansive levels for pieces.<ref>{{cite video game|title=Sonic Adventure|developer=Sonic Team|publisher=Sega|date=September 9, 1999|quote=Knuckles: It's up to me to find the missing pieces of the Master Emerald.}}</ref> At one point, he defeats Chaos,<ref>{{cite video game|title=Sonic Adventure|developer=Sonic Team|publisher=Sega|date=September 9, 1999|quote=Knuckles: It's that creature again! The same one I saw on my island.}}</ref> and Eggman tricks Knuckles into thinking that Sonic is trying to collect Emerald shards for his own purposes.<ref>{{cite video game|title=Sonic Adventure|developer=Sonic Team|publisher=Sega|date=September 9, 1999|quote=Eggman: He's after the pieces of the Master Emerald, too!}}</ref> Knuckles finds Sonic holding two Chaos Emeralds he thinks are Master Emerald shards, and attacks him.<ref>{{cite video game|title=Sonic Adventure|developer=Sonic Team|publisher=Sega|date=September 9, 1999|quote=Knuckles: All right! Put 'em up! Hand over the Emerald now!}}</ref> This knocks them out of Sonic's hands,<ref>{{cite video game|title=Sonic Adventure|developer=Sonic Team|publisher=Sega|date=September 9, 1999|quote=Sonic: Oh no! The Chaos Emeralds...!}}</ref> so Eggman shows up to steal them and leaves.<ref>{{cite video game|title=Sonic Adventure|developer=Sonic Team|publisher=Sega|date=September 9, 1999|quote=Eggman: Ha! That's all there is to it. You guys are too easy!}}</ref> He initially stays on Earth to look for pieces while Sonic and [[Tails (Sonic the Hedgehog)|Tails]] follow Eggman,<ref>{{cite video game|title=Sonic Adventure|developer=Sonic Team|publisher=Sega|date=September 9, 1999|quote=Sonic: No problem, Knuckles! We'll take care of everything here.}}</ref> but later joins them aboard Eggman's airship, the Egg Carrier, after seeing a vision of there being more pieces on it.<ref>{{cite video game|title=Sonic Adventure|developer=Sonic Team|publisher=Sega|date=September 9, 1999|quote=Knuckles: Hey look! It's Eggman's flying fortress. That's where the rest of the pieces must be.}}</ref> He finds the final pieces and is confronted by Chaos' final form,<ref>{{cite video game|title=Sonic Adventure|developer=Sonic Team|publisher=Sega|date=September 9, 1999|quote=Knuckles: No! It can't be! I guess he didn't get enough the first time!}}</ref> then returns to the Emerald's island to restore it.<ref>{{cite video game|title=Sonic Adventure|developer=Sonic Team|publisher=Sega|date=September 9, 1999|quote=Knuckles: This should do it! Perfect. All is well, now! The Master Emerald and the island have been restored.}}</ref>

Early in ''[[Sonic Adventure 2]]'', Knuckles and [[Rouge the Bat|Rouge]] argue over the Emerald;<ref>{{cite video game|title=[[Sonic Adventure 2]]|developer=[[Sega Studio USA]]|publisher=Sega|date=June 19, 2001|quote=Knuckles: What are you talking about? That Emerald's mine!}}</ref> she wants the pieces for her personal collection. Eggman tries to steal it,<ref>{{cite video game|title=Sonic Adventure 2|developer=Sega Studio USA|publisher=Sega|date=June 19, 2001|quote=Rouge: Whaa... thief!}}</ref> so Knuckles shatters it aboard Eggman's hovercraft, sending the pieces every which way, while also mentioning that if the shards are found they can be made whole. He spends the game recollecting the pieces like in ''Adventure''.<ref>{{cite video game|title=Sonic Adventure 2|developer=Sega Studio USA|publisher=Sega|date=June 19, 2001|quote=Knuckles: I did that to prevent the Master Emerald from being stolen, you idiot! If it's in pieces, I can restore it.}}</ref> He later helps Sonic, Tails, and Amy find Eggman's base inside a [[Egyptian pyramids|giant pyramid]]<ref>{{cite video game|title=Sonic Adventure 2|developer=Sega Studio USA|publisher=Sega|date=June 19, 2001|quote=Knuckles: I saw Eggman go inside the pyramid and more importantly, I saw that bat go inside with him as well.}}</ref> and a key to an inner chamber housing a giant [[Space Shuttle]].<ref>{{cite video game|title=Sonic Adventure 2|developer=Sega Studio USA|publisher=Sega|date=June 19, 2001|quote=Knuckles: What? Why do I have to find the key?}}</ref> He follows them to a giant space station called the ARK with it, where he again scuffles with Rouge over the Emerald.<ref>{{cite video game|title=Sonic Adventure 2|developer=Sega Studio USA|publisher=Sega|date=June 19, 2001|quote=Knuckles and Rouge in unison: Stop fooling around, and give me back MY Emeralds!}}</ref> He saves her from falling into a constructed pit of [[lava]];<ref>{{cite video game|title=Sonic Adventure 2|developer=Sega Studio USA|publisher=Sega|date=June 19, 2001|quote=Rouge: Keep your hands to yourself! Don't touch me!}}</ref> she decides the shards are worthless and dismissively lets him keep them,<ref>{{cite video game|title=Sonic Adventure 2|developer=Sega Studio USA|publisher=Sega|date=June 19, 2001|quote=Rouge: Fine, just take them. They stink like echidnas do.}}</ref> so he reassembles the Emerald and runs off.<ref>{{cite video game|title=Sonic Adventure 2|developer=Sega Studio USA|publisher=Sega|date=June 19, 2001|quote=Knuckles: Finally.}}</ref><ref>{{cite video game|title=Sonic Adventure 2|developer=Sega Studio USA|publisher=Sega|date=June 19, 2001|quote=Rouge: We should get going.}}</ref> The antagonist [[Gerald Robotnik]], Eggman's grandfather, initiates a program to send the ARK on a collision course with Earth as revenge for an attack on the ARK decades earlier,<ref>{{cite video game|title=Sonic Adventure 2|developer=Sega Studio USA|publisher=Sega|date=June 19, 2001|quote=Gerald: All of you humans who took everything away from me will feel my loss and despair!}}</ref> so Knuckles teams up with the other playable characters to reroute it.<ref>{{cite video game|title=Sonic Adventure 2|developer=Sega Studio USA|publisher=Sega|date=June 19, 2001|quote=Knuckles: That's right. If I use this, we just might be able to stop the Chaos Emerald!}}</ref>

Knuckles serves as a power-based character in ''[[Sonic Heroes]]'' alongside Sonic and Tails, who respectively represent speed and flight.<ref name="heroes 7">''Sonic Heroes'' (GameCube) instruction manual, p. 7.</ref> They team up to defeat Eggman after receiving a letter saying that he will destroy the world in three days.<ref>{{cite video game|title=[[Sonic Heroes]]|developer=Sonic Team USA|publisher=Sega|date=January 5, 2004|quote=Eggman: In 3 days, I will conquer the world. Think you can stop me?}}</ref> However, it turns out that Eggman is being impersonated by [[Metal Sonic]], whom all of the other characters defeat together.<ref>{{cite video game|title=Sonic Heroes|developer=Sonic Team USA|publisher=Sega|date=January 5, 2004|quote=Eggman: Aaaa... If only we had the 7 Chaos Emeralds!}}</ref> Knuckles helps Sonic, Tails, [[Amy Rose]], and [[Cream the Rabbit]] stop Eggman from building an empire in the ''[[Sonic Advance]]'' [[Sonic Advance 3|trilogy]].<ref>''[[Sonic Advance]]'' (Game Boy Advance) instruction manual, p. 4.</ref><ref>''[[Sonic Advance 2]]'' instruction manual, p. 4.</ref><ref>''[[Sonic Advance 3]]'' instruction manual, p. 12.</ref> With the same team, Knuckles recurs in ''[[Sonic Riders]]'' and its two sequels; in each game, they participate in board-racing competitions together.<ref>{{cite video game|title=[[Sonic Riders]]|developer=Sonic Team|publisher=Sega|date=February 21, 2006|quote=Knuckles: (about [[Wave the Swallow]]) Did she say red MUTT?!}}</ref><ref>{{cite video game|title=[[Sonic Riders: Zero Gravity]]|developer=Sonic Team|publisher=Sega|date=January 8, 2008|quote=Knuckles: Anytime... Babylon Rogues.}}</ref><ref>{{cite video game|title=[[Sonic Free Riders]]|developer=Sonic Team|publisher=Sega|date=November 4, 2010|quote=Knuckles: Step aside!}}</ref> In another team-based installment, the [[role-playing video game|role-playing game]] ''[[Sonic Chronicles: The Dark Brotherhood]]'', Knuckles is a playable character with a major role in the story. The game begins with Tails informing Sonic that Knuckles has been kidnapped, so a team beginning as Sonic, Tails, Amy, and Rouge must rescue him. He is eventually saved, and it is revealed that the echidna race is still alive in the form of the helpful Shade the Echidna and her villainous tribe, the Nocturnus.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gamespot.com/reviews/sonic-chronicles-the-dark-brotherhood-review/1900-6199160/|website=[[GameSpot]]|last=Stella|first=Shiva|title=Sonic Chronicles: The Dark Brotherhood Review|date=October 10, 2008|access-date=October 26, 2014|archive-date=May 19, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140519181742/http://www.gamespot.com/reviews/sonic-chronicles-the-dark-brotherhood-review/1900-6199160/|url-status=live}}</ref>

He is a minor character in ''[[Sonic Rush]]'',<ref name="bright">{{cite video game|title=[[Sonic Rush]]|developer=Sonic Team|publisher=Sega|date=November 15, 2005|quote=Cream: He's a tough guy, but he isn't very bright.)}}</ref> where he accosts [[Blaze the Cat]] under the impression that she has stolen Chaos Emeralds.<ref>{{cite video game|title=Sonic Rush|developer=Sonic Team|publisher=Sega|date=November 15, 2005|quote=Knuckles: I can sense their power here!}}</ref> In the [[Nintendo DS]] version of ''[[Sonic Colors]]'', Knuckles arrives at an amusement park Eggman has created after receiving a letter.<ref>{{cite video game|title=[[Sonic Colors]] (Nintendo DS)|developer=Sonic Team|publisher=Sega|date=November 16, 2010|quote=Rouge: Are you saying you didn't come here because of one of Eggman's letters?}}</ref> Frustrated at having been tricked,<ref>{{cite video game|title=Sonic Colors (Nintendo DS)|developer=Sonic Team|publisher=Sega|date=November 16, 2010|quote=Tails: So, um, Knuckles? ===In comics===
In ''[[Sonic the Comic]]'', Knuckles plays a similar role to that of the games. When the Death Egg crashes on Angel Island, Knuckles is briefly tricked by Dr. Robotnik<ref>{{cite comic|story=Knuckles: Guardian of the Chaos Emeralds|title=[[Sonic the Comic]]|issue=N/A ("Sonic Holiday Special 1994")|date=June 18, 1994 |publisher=[[Egmont Publishing]]}}</ref> and thus allows Robotnik to place his robot armies on the island and construct a base to repair his Death Egg.<ref>{{cite comic|story=Robotnik's Revenge, Part 1|title=Sonic the Comic|issue=37|date=October 28, 1994|publisher=Egmont Publishing}}</ref> Knuckles also assists him in fighting Sonic and stealing Sonic's own six Emeralds so they can be combined with Knuckles's into one set of Emeralds.<ref>{{cite comic|story=Power of the Chaos Emeralds, Part 1|title=Sonic the Comic|issue=35|date=September 30, 1994|publisher=Egmont Publishing}}</ref> However, Knuckles does not trust Robotnik enough to tell him that he possesses a seventh Emerald that can control the others, and when Robotnik tries to absorb the Emeralds' power into himself, Knuckles uses this Emerald to defeat him.<ref>{{cite comic|story=Power of the Chaos Emeralds, Part 2|title=Sonic the Comic|issue=36|date=October 13, 1994|publisher=Egmont Publishing}}</ref> From that point on, he works as an ally against Robotnik, starting by removing all traces of the doctor's influences from Angel Island.<ref>{{cite comic|story=Carnival Night Conspiracy, Part 1|title=Sonic the Comic|issue=39|date=November 25, 1994|publisher=Egmont Publishing}}</ref>

In the [[Sonic the Hedgehog (comics)|comic series of ''Sonic the Hedgehog'']] published by [[Archie Comics]], Knuckles is the eighteenth guardian of the Floating Island, which is also called Angel Island. He is also a member of the [[Brotherhood of Guardians]], a [[secret society]] that defends the island and is made up of Knuckles's predecessors/ancestors. In keeping with the incorporation of elements of the [[Sonic the Hedgehog (TV series)|''Sonic the Hedgehog'']] cartoon into the series, Knuckles lives on the planet Mobius. Knuckles is supported in his efforts by the [[Chaotix]], and often works together with Sonic the Hedgehog and the Freedom Fighters.<ref name="auto7">{{cite book|last1=Bollers|first1=Karl|last2=Penders|first2=Ken|title=Archie Sonic the Hedgehog Issue 131|date=December 2003|publisher=Archie Comics|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|last=Penders|first=Ken|title=Archie Knuckles the Echidna Issue 1|date=January 1997|publisher=Archie Comics|language=en}}</ref>

In the intercompany crossover miniseries ''[[DC X Sonic the Hedgehog]]'', Knuckles is among Sonic's friends who join forces with the Justice League to stop Darkseid from conquering their universe with the Chaos Emeralds. Knuckles becomes mainly partnered with [[Superman]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Scullion |first1=Chris |title=DC x Sonic the Hedgehog: Here's the first art and plot details from Sega and DC's crossover comic |url=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/news/dc-x-sonic-the-hedgehog-heres-the-first-art-and-plot-details-from-sega-and-dcs-crossover-comic/ |website=[[Video Games Chronicle]] |access-date=March 19, 2025 |date=March 13, 2025}}</ref>

===In animation===
Knuckles's animation debut came with the 1996 Japanese ''[[Sonic the Hedgehog (OVA)|Sonic the Hedgehog]]'' [[original video animation|OVA]]. Sonic and Tails meet him during their trip into the Land of Darkness, and over the course of the film he helps them defeat Black Eggman/Metal Robotnik and [[Metal Sonic|Hyper Metal Sonic]], two robots created by Eggman/Robotnik. As Metal is about to descend into a lava pit, Sonic attempts to save him after all, but Knuckles holds him back and Sonic is disappointed. Knuckles play-fights with Sonic a few times in the film as well.<ref>{{cite AV media|title=[[Sonic the Hedgehog (OVA)|Sonic the Hedgehog: The Movie]]|year=1999|publisher=[[ADV Films]]|medium=DVD}}</ref>

Knuckles is a minor character in ''[[Sonic Underground]]''. Sonic, Sonia, and Manic meet Knuckles atop his home, the Floating Island, while searching for their mother. Knuckles is initially skeptical of them but soon accepts their help in protecting the Island and its guardian Chaos Emerald from villains Sleet and Dingo.<ref>{{cite episode|title=Friend or Foe?|episode-link=List of Sonic Underground episodes|series=[[Sonic Underground]]|airdate=January 18, 2000|season=1|number=18}}</ref> Later on, the siblings recruit Knuckles to help them deactivate Doctor Robotnik's giant fortress, as it is powered by Emeralds and he can control them.<ref>{{cite episode|title=Flying Fortress|episode-link=List of Sonic Underground episodes|series=Sonic Underground|airdate=March 22, 2000|season=1|number=27}}</ref> They succeed, but Sleet and Dingo accidentally break the Emerald, unleashing gradually effective but massive energy upon the planet Mobius, and Knuckles enlists one of his relatives to help them control it, with mediocre results.<ref>{{cite episode|title=No Hedgehog Is an Island|episode-link=List of Sonic Underground episodes|series=Sonic Underground|airdate=March 29, 2000|season=1|number=28}}</ref> Reluctantly, Knuckles cuts a deal with Robotnik to turn over the hedgehogs in exchange for setting Mobius right; Robotnik succeeds and starts turning the hedgehogs into robots, but Knuckles betrays Robotnik to rescue his friends.<ref>{{cite episode|title=New Echidna in Town|episode-link=List of Sonic Underground episodes|series=Sonic Underground|airdate=April 5, 2000|season=1|number=29}}</ref>

Knuckles appears in all three seasons of ''[[Sonic X]]'', where he is depicted as the guardian of the Master Emerald, and is said to have a "chip on his shoulder". The Sonic X version of Knuckles has been described as an "incredibly serious warrior with a deep, fleshed-out backstory" in comparison to the more comedic depictions of the character in recent years.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pitman |first=Robert |date=2024-04-28 |title=If You Liked Knuckles, Check This Underrated Sonic The Hedgehog Show From 21 Years Ago |url=https://screenrant.com/knuckles-sonic-x-animated-show-good-watch/ |access-date=2024-10-27 |website=ScreenRant |language=en}}</ref> After being stranded in the new world with Sonic, his only desire is to get back home quickly.<ref name="4Kids characters">{{cite web |url=http://www.4kids.tv/show/sonic-x/characters |title=Characters: Knuckles|access-date=October 26, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120410060055/http://www.4kids.tv/show/sonic-x/characters|archive-date=April 10, 2012|publisher=4Kids.tv}}</ref>

Knuckles is among the main cast in the ''[[Sonic Boom (TV series)|Sonic Boom]]'' animated series, and had been redesigned for it: now being taller and more muscular than before.<ref name="scarf"/> His Intelligence has regressed, as he become opposite of his original self.

Knuckles appears as a supporting character in ''[[Sonic Prime]]''. After Sonic shatters the Paradox Prism, which results in the creation of multiple parallel dimensions at the expense of his own, multiple versions of Knuckles are made as well; such as Renegade Knucks who is a rebel against the Chaos Council of New Yoke City, the feral and paranoid Gnarly, and the pirate captain Knuckles the Dread. Knuckles is voiced by Adam Nurada and his variants are voiced by [[Vincent Tong (voice actor)|Vincent Tong]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Griffin |first=David |date=October 27, 2022 |title=Sonic Prime: Exclusive Release Date and Character Posters Reveal for Netflix Animated Series |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/sonic-prime-release-date-character-posters-netflix |access-date=October 27, 2022 |website=IGN |language=en |archive-date=October 30, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221030123816/https://www.ign.com/articles/sonic-prime-release-date-character-posters-netflix |url-status=live }}</ref>

===In other media===
While Knuckles does not appear in the Sonic series's first theatrical film, ''[[Sonic the Hedgehog (film)|Sonic the Hedgehog]]'', his existence is alluded to within the film's opening sequence in which a young Sonic and his caretaker Longclaw are attacked by a native clan of Echidnas.

Knuckles appears alongside Sonic and Tails in the [[Sonic the Hedgehog 2 (film)|second film]], voiced by [[Idris Elba]]. In the film, it is revealed he is the last of the Echidna Tribe, as the rest of his kind became critically endangered and are in terminal decline due to a war between them and the giant owls, and has a grudge against Sonic for being Longclaw's apprentice. After being informed of Sonic's location by Dr. Robotnik, he teams up with the scientist and travels to Earth to defeat Sonic and seek out the Master Emerald to honor his ancestors. At the temple where the Emerald is located, Robotnik betrays Knuckles and leaves him to die, but he is rescued by Sonic. He teams up with Sonic and Tails to defeat Robotnik in Green Hills and reclaim the Master Emerald. The three agree to safeguard the Emerald as they live with Sonic's adoptive Earth family, the Wachowskis.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Knuckles Seemingly Confirmed for Sonic 2|url=https://comicbook.com/gaming/news/knuckles-sonic-the-hedgehog-2-leaked-set-photos/|access-date=2021-04-24|website=Gaming|date=21 April 2021 |language=en|archive-date=2021-04-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210424160744/https://comicbook.com/gaming/news/knuckles-sonic-the-hedgehog-2-leaked-set-photos/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="TheWrap"/>

Knuckles is the titular primary protagonist of a [[Knuckles (TV series)|spinoff miniseries of the same name]] released on [[Paramount+]], with Elba reprising the role. In the miniseries, Knuckles (who is struggling to adjust to his new life and home on Earth) takes deputy sheriff Wade Whipple in as his "apprentice", training him in the ways of the Echidna warrior to help him prepare for a bowling tournament in [[Reno, Nevada]] where his estranged father will be competing. During their journey, Wade is reunited with his mother and sister, while Knuckles is pursued by "the Buyer", Dr. Robotnik's former operative who seeks to take Knuckles's power for himself.<ref name=":0b">{{Cite web|last=Kroll|first=Justin|date=2022-02-15|title='Sonic The Hedgehog' Universe Continues To Grow As Sega And Paramount Sign Off On Third Film As Well As A 'Knuckles' Spin-Off Series In The Works At Paramount+ With Idris Elba Reprising Role|url=https://deadline.com/2022/02/sonic-the-hedgehog-sega-paramount-third-installment-knuckles-spin-off-series-idris-elba-1234933921/|access-date=2022-02-15|website=Deadline|language=en-US|archive-date=2022-02-15|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220215220856/https://deadline.com/2022/02/sonic-the-hedgehog-sega-paramount-third-installment-knuckles-spin-off-series-idris-elba-1234933921/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Knuckles appears alongside Sonic and Tails in ''[[Sonic the Hedgehog 3 (film)|Sonic the Hedgehog 3]]'', with Elba reprising the role, again. Knuckles continues to live with Sonic and Tails, with the Wachowskis, serving as the "muscle" of their team when they try to stop Shadow the Hedgehog. Knuckles continues to safeguard the Master Emerald with Wade's assistance until Sonic forces them to give him the Emerald, to use its powers to defeat Shadow. Knuckles continues to tend to go into confrontations eager to fight, or at least break something, but continues to remain loyal and even tries to give supportive advice to Sonic.

==Reception and impact==
The character has received positive attention. According to ''[[IGN]]''{{'}}s Levi Buchanan, fans "seemed legitimately happy" with the addition of the character of Knuckles, who was popular enough to get marquee billing in ''[[Sonic & Knuckles]]'', but Buchanan felt that characters who came after him were going "overboard".<ref name="IGN wrong">{{cite web |url=http://retro.ign.com/articles/955/955741p2.html |title=Where Did Sonic Go Wrong? |last=Buchanan |first=Levi |date=February 20, 2009 |access-date=October 26, 2014 |archive-date=August 31, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110831064313/http://retro.ign.com/articles/955/955741p2.html |url-status=live }}</ref> IGN's Colin Moriarty singled out the introduction of both Knuckles and Tails as when the series became "iffy" and listed them and all other characters in the series, sans Sonic and Robotnik, as being 2nd most in need to "die" on his top 10 list.<ref name="IGN die">{{cite web|author1=IGN PlayStation Team|author2=Moriarty, Colin|date=February 18, 2009|title=Wednesday 10: Video game Characters That Should Die|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2009/02/18/wednesday-10-videogame-characters-that-should-die-2?amp=1|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110613191707/http://pc.ign.com/articles/955/955079p1.html|archive-date=June 13, 2011|access-date=October 26, 2014}}</ref> In contrast, he was listed as the best ''Sonic'' character by ''[[Official Nintendo Magazine]]'' based on the impact he brought to the ''Sonic'' games in which he first appeared.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.officialnintendomagazine.co.uk/50022/features/the-best-and-worst-sonic-characters/?page=5|title=The best and worst Sonic characters|magazine=[[Official Nintendo Magazine]]|last=East|first=Thomas|access-date=October 24, 2013|date=May 29, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029204405/http://www.officialnintendomagazine.co.uk/50022/features/the-best-and-worst-sonic-characters/?page=5|archive-date=October 29, 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> Similarly, ''[[Complex (magazine)|Complex]]'' writer Elijah Watson considers him a better character than Sonic. Watson praises his debut in ''[[Sonic the Hedgehog 3]]'', and adds "Knuckles could have never been Sega's mascot; the echidna lacks the sociability of Sonic and his Nintendo counterpart, Mario. And yet this defining characteristic is what makes him so appealing. He is Sega's anti-hero: the dreadlocked brawler who is surprisingly selfless and has a soft spot for grapes and adorable animals."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.complex.com/pop-culture/2014/02/knuckles-is-better-than-sonic-definitive-reasoning-20-year-anniversary-sonic-the-hedgehog-3 |title=Knuckles is Better Than Sonic: A Definitive Reasoning on the 20 Year Anniversary of "Sonic The Hedgehog 3" |last=Watson |first=Elijah |date=February 5, 2014 |work=Complex |access-date=April 17, 2022 |archive-date=April 18, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220418023947/https://www.complex.com/pop-culture/2014/02/knuckles-is-better-than-sonic-definitive-reasoning-20-year-anniversary-sonic-the-hedgehog-3 |url-status=live }}</ref>

In an official 2006 poll by Sonic Team, Knuckles was the fourth most popular character in the series, following behind [[Miles "Tails" Prower|Tails]], [[Shadow the Hedgehog|Shadow]], and Sonic.<ref>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120229160623/http://sonic.sega.jp/SonicChannel/event/016/002.html|archive-date=February 29, 2012|url=http://sonic.sega.jp/SonicChannel/event/016/002.html|script-title=ja:ソニックチャンネル/イベント/ソニック キャラクター 人気投票 結果発表！|language=ja|access-date=October 26, 2014|date=June 23, 2006}}</ref> Knuckles was ranked fifth in a later 2025 popularity poll by ''[[Dengeki Online]]''.<ref>{{cite web |title=The results of the "Sonic" character popularity poll have been announced! (Wii U/3DS)|Super Smash Bros.]]'' game.<ref>{{cite magazine |url=http://www.complex.com/video-games/2012/07/25-characters-we-want-to-see-in-super-smash-bros-brawl-4/knuckles-the-echidna |title=Knuckles the Echidna – 25 Characters We Want To See In "Super Smash Bros. ===Ugandan Knuckles===
[[File:Ugandan Knuckles.png|thumb|This deformed version of Knuckles by YouTube user Gregzilla became the basis for "Ugandan Knuckles", which had a brief surge of popularity in early 2018.]]
In late December 2017, players began to flood the virtual reality video game ''[[VRChat]]'' with avatars depicting a deformed version of the character called "Ugandan Knuckles". The character stemmed from a 2017 review of ''[[Sonic Lost World]]'' by [[YouTube]] user Gregzilla as well as from fans of ''[[PlayerUnknown's Battlegrounds]]'' streamer [[Forsen]] who often make references to [[Uganda]] in the chat section of his streams. The character is often associated with quotes such as "Do you know da wae?" and "Save the queen!" among many other quotes, which originate from the 2010 Ugandan action comedy film ''[[Who Killed Captain Alex?]]'' as well as for "spitting" on other users whom they feel do not know "da wae".<ref name="daily dot">{{Cite web|url=https://www.dailydot.com/unclick/ugandan-knuckles-vrchat-meme/|title=How Ugandan Knuckles turned VRChat into a total trollfest|last=Hathaway|first=Jay|date=11 January 2018|website=The Daily Dot|access-date=13 January 2018|archive-date=14 January 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180114183924/https://www.dailydot.com/unclick/ugandan-knuckles-vrchat-meme/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://heavy.com/games/2018/01/controversial-ugandan-knuckles-meme/|title=Controversial 'Ugandan Knuckles' Meme Has Infested VRChat|last=MacGregor|first=Collin|date=9 January 2018|website=Heavy.com|access-date=13 January 2018|archive-date=9 January 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180109225822/https://heavy.com/games/2018/01/controversial-ugandan-knuckles-meme/|url-status=live}}</ref>

The meme was criticized by some journalists as being racially insensitive;<ref name="daily dot" /><ref name=Polygon2/> ''Polygon'' described it as "problematic".<ref name=Polygon2>{{cite web|url=https://www.polygon.com/2018/1/8/16863932/ugandan-knuckles-meme-vrchat|title='Ugandan Knuckles' is overtaking VRChat|last=Alexander|first=Julia|publisher=[[Vox Media, Inc.]]|work=Polygon|date=January 8, 2018|access-date=January 9, 2018|archive-date=January 8, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180108233545/https://www.polygon.com/2018/1/8/16863932/ugandan-knuckles-meme-vrchat|url-status=live}}</ref> The creator of the avatar, [[DeviantArt]] user "tidiestflyer", has expressed regret over how it has been used, in particular saying that he hopes it is not used to annoy players of ''VRChat'', and that he enjoys the game and he does not want to see anyone's rights get taken away because of the avatar.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.gamerevolution.com/news/362289-creator-vrchats-ugandan-knuckles-meme-regrets-decision|title=Creator of VRChat's 'Ugandan Knuckles' Meme Regrets His Decision|last=Tamburro|first=Paul|date=8 January 2018|website=GameRevolution|access-date=13 January 2018|archive-date=10 January 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180110005557/http://www.gamerevolution.com/news/362289-creator-vrchats-ugandan-knuckles-meme-regrets-decision|url-status=live}}</ref> In response, in January 2018 the developers of ''VRChat'' published an open letter on ''[[Medium (website)|Medium]]'', stating that they were developing "new systems to allow the community to better self-moderate" and asking users to use the built-in muting features.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.polygon.com/2018/1/10/16875716/vrchat-safety-concerns-open-letter-players-behavior |title=VRChat team speaks up on player harassment in open letter |last=Alexander |first=Julia |date=January 10, 2018 |website=Polygon |access-date=May 21, 2022 |archive-date=January 11, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180111044359/https://www.polygon.com/2018/1/10/16875716/vrchat-safety-concerns-open-letter-players-behavior |url-status=live }}</ref>

In April 2019, Canadian toy company [[Youtooz]] launched their line of [[Polyvinyl chloride|vinyl]] collectible [[figurine]]s with a depiction of Ugandan Knuckles.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Weimer |first1=Jackson |title=Youtooz: Holding The Internet's Creators And Memes In Your Hand |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/jacksonweimer/2021/06/24/youtooz-holding-the-internets--creators-and-memes-in-your-hand/ |website=Forbes |access-date=8 May 2024 |language=en}}</ref>

===...& Knuckles===
Another Knuckles-centric meme is derived from the video game ''[[Sonic & Knuckles|Sonic 3 & Knuckles]]'', a game which combined ''[[Sonic the Hedgehog 3]]'' and ''Sonic & Knuckles'', accessed by attaching the cartridge of the former to the latter. The awkward-sounding combination of names resulted in a meme where a fictitious and absurdly long video game name is created (usually one for a long-running franchise) with "& Knuckles" appended to the end of it. This meme was also used to poke fun at the [[Nintendo DS]] and [[Nintendo 3DS]] series of systems due to the large number of variants, with & Knuckles often appended to the end of an invented system, e.g. "New Nintendo 3DSi XL & Knuckles".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://knowyourmeme.com/memes/knuckles |website=Know Your Meme |access-date=27 August 2024 |title=& Knuckles |date=26 December 2014 }}</ref> This was later referenced in ''[[Sonic Mania]]'', which featured an unlockable "& Knuckles" mode, allowing a computer-controlled Knuckles to follow the player's character, even if Knuckles is also chosen as the playable character.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Frank |first=Allegra |date=August 15, 2017 |title=Sonic Mania's secret mode is Sega embracing fans' favorite joke |url=https://www.polygon.com/2017/8/15/16151720/sonic-mania-secret-mode |website=Polygon}}</ref>

{{IPA|de|ˈedvart|lang}} | gender = Male | meaning = ''[[wikt:ead#Old English|ēad]]'' "Riches", "Prosperous" or "Fortune" and ''[[wikt:weard#Old English|weard]]'' "Guardian" or "Protector" | region = | origin = [[Old English]]: ''Ēadweard'' | related names = [[Eduard (name)|Eduard]], [[Édouard]], [[Edoardo]], [[Edvard]], [[Eduardas]], [[Edvardas]], [[Eduardo]], [[Edwin]], [[Eddie (given name)|Eddie]], [[Ed (given name)|Ed]], [[Edd (disambiguation)#people|Edd]], [[Edith]], [[Duarte (name)|Duarte]], [[Ned (given name)|Ned]], [[Odoardo]], [[Ted (given name)|Ted]], [[Ward (given name)|Ward]], [[Woody (name)|Woody]] | footnotes = }} '''Edward''' is an [[English language|English]] masculine name. It is derived from the [[Old English|Anglo-Saxon]] name ''Ēadweard'', composed of the elements ''[[wikt:ead#Old English|ēad]]'' "wealth, fortune; prosperity" and ''[[wikt:weard#Old English|weard]]'' "guardian, protector”. ==History== The name Edward was very popular in Anglo-Saxon England, but the rule of the [[House of Normandy|Norman]] and [[House of Plantagenet|Plantagenet]] dynasties had effectively ended its use amongst the upper classes.{{cite book |title=The Plantagenets: The Warrior Kings and Queens Who Made England |first1=Dan |last1=Jones |author-link=Dan Jones (writer) |date=25 March 2014 |publisher=Penguin Books |isbn=978-0-14-312492-4 |page=241}} The popularity of the name was revived when [[Henry III of England|Henry III]] named his firstborn son, the future [[Edward I]], as part of his efforts to promote a cult around [[Edward the Confessor]], for whom Henry had a deep admiration.{{cite book |title=The Plantagenets: The Warrior Kings and Queens Who Made England |first1=Dan |last1=Jones |author-link=Dan Jones (writer) |date=25 March 2014 |publisher=Penguin Books |isbn=978-0-14-312492-4 |pages=241–242}} ==Variant forms== {{Wiktionary|Edward#Translations}} The name has been adopted in the [[Iberian Peninsula#Modern Iberia|Iberian peninsula]] since the 15th century, due to [[Edward, King of Portugal]], whose mother was English. The Spanish/Portuguese forms of the name are [[Eduardo]] and [[Duarte (name)|Duarte]]. Other variant forms include French [[Édouard]], Italian [[Edoardo]] and [[Odoardo]], German, Dutch, Czech and Romanian [[Eduard (name)|Eduard]] and Scandinavian [[Edvard]].
